detection.notes: Archived bagakit-ft rows remain historical implementation evidence. The active backlog is now a manual review-derived kernel hardening/test plan created on 2026-03-24 to restore green quality gates and close uncovered core risks.

rows.title: Restore lint/check gate and remove stale orchestrator helpers
rows.why_now: `make check` is currently red on staticcheck findings, so the project's default evidence gate is already broken before any new kernel work begins.
acceptance_criteria: `make lint` exits 0 with no SA1012/SA4000/U1000 findings.
The fixed assertions still verify the intended behavior instead of weakening test coverage.
evidence: `make lint` fails on SA1012 at pkg/adapter/localfs/adapter_behavior_test.go:238 because the test passes a nil context.
`make lint` fails on SA4000 at pkg/engine/engine_test.go:1952 because the jsonl assertion compares the same expression twice.
`make lint` fails on U1000 for three unused helpers in pkg/engine/orchestrator.go:536-557, and `make check` inherits the same failure.
risks: Keep the change surgical: restore the gate without changing command-dispatch semantics.
If any removed helper is still conceptually needed, reintroduce it only with a live call site and regression coverage.

rows.title: Add direct package tests for agentfs zone behavior and pathguard escapes
rows.why_now: The default workspace trust story depends on `agentfs` and `pathguard`, but those packages still have zero direct package coverage even though they own zone resolution and path-escape prevention.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./pkg/adapter/agentfs ./pkg/adapter/internal/pathguard` passes with new direct tests.
Tests cover writable vs read-only zones, path normalization, metadata shaping, and symlink or missing-ancestor escape rejection.
Integration sanity remains green under `go test ./pkg/fs ./pkg/engine`.
evidence: Coverage output shows `pkg/adapter/agentfs` at 0.0% even though `pkg/fs.NewAIFilesystem` delegates the default runtime zones to it.
Coverage output shows `pkg/adapter/internal/pathguard` at 0.0% even though `agentfs.toHostPath()` relies on it for escape prevention.
Current `pkg/fs` tests exercise some integration regressions, but low-level `DescribePath`, `PathEnv`, zone walking, and `resolveWithExistingPrefix()` invariants are not package-local locked.
risks: Avoid duplicating the full integration harness; target the low-level invariants that can regress silently.
If direct tests expose a real bug, patch the production code in the same smallest closure instead of papering over the failure.

rows.title: Harden parser and redirection regressions around heredoc and edge-case script syntax
rows.why_now: The parser and script runner are core kernel surfaces, but heredoc branches and several parser failure paths remain effectively unexercised, which makes shell-level regressions easy to miss.
acceptance_criteria: New engine tests cover heredoc success plus failure cases such as missing delimiters or unclosed quotes.
Redirection edge tests cover write or append behavior without introducing partial side effects or unexpected exit-code changes.
`go test ./pkg/engine ./pkg/sh` passes, and `go test ./...` stays green.
evidence: A repo search over engine tests shows no heredoc-specific coverage even though the parser implements `<<` support.
Coverage output leaves `readHereDocBody()` and multiple parser error branches only partially covered.
These branches live in the kernel execution path, so a parser regression would hit the common inspect-edit-test loop directly.
risks: Keep the shell surface stable; start with tests and only change semantics when a failing regression proves the need.
Do not broaden shell compatibility beyond the documented subset while adding coverage.

rows.title: Close regression gaps in HTTP and CLI entry surfaces
rows.why_now: Entry adapters are not the architecture center, but they are still public integration surfaces; current coverage misses serve-mode branches, service wrappers, and include-meta fallback edges.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./cmd/simsh-cli ./pkg/service/httpapi ./pkg/service` passes with new regression coverage.
Tests cover session error/status mapping and at least one `include_meta` path that exercises mount or synthetic-path metadata fallback behavior.
CLI tests cover serve-mode option normalization or root fallback without relying on a long-lived network listener.
evidence: Coverage output shows 0.0% on `pkg/service/service.go`, which is a public wrapper surface for library-style callers.
Coverage output shows 0.0% on `cmd/simsh-cli` serve-mode helpers such as `runServe()` and root-resolution branches.
`describePathMetaViaLS()` in `pkg/service/httpapi/execute_endpoint.go` remains unexecuted, leaving the metadata fallback path effectively unverified.
risks: Keep tests deterministic and non-blocking; do not add network flake just to raise coverage.
If fallback metadata is dead code, either prove it with tests or remove it explicitly rather than leaving an unowned branch.
